milestones.title: Published Fawn release
milestones.summary: Fawn is the local-first persistent private browser product candidate. The Linux x64 release-candidate lane is governed alongside macOS arm64, but no platform has yet produced a clean-install, forced-Doe, exact-oracle release candidate, and product promotion remains subject to the separate K0 external comparison.

evidence.description: Complete archive, launch, identity, fallback, proof-surface, and receipt contract.
Governed release platforms and required platform package members.
Schema for governed release platforms and package support members.
Release package preflight including Linux ELF identity, build profile, and runtime support members.
Deterministic archive packer that requires eligible Linux candidate preflight evidence.
Safe isolated archive extraction plus packaged-browser launch and forced Dawn/Doe smoke verification.
Schema for observational clean-install release evidence.
K0 comparison and eligibility law kept separate from the A/B/C/D causal matrix.
Schema-backed K0 Quick Action and CDP admission table that retains unsupported workloads as ineligible.
Cloudflare Browser Run plus Kitesurf executor with caller-bound exact response oracles and no internal component credit.
Connector test proving admitted execution, explicit ineligibility, exact-oracle failure, and non-promotion.
Historical compact diagnostic archive manifest path; the ignored artifact is not retained locally and grants no evidence.
Governed isolated-install verifier result for the retained compact archive, including exact missing package members.

exitCriteria: A cleanly extracted release-candidate archive launches on its declared platform.
Forced Doe is hash-bound, adapter hardware identity is visible, and hidden fallback is absent.
One unchanged application passes an independent oracle plus reload, teardown, concurrency, and memory-growth checks.
Any promoted advantage uses matched browser builds, work, timing scope, and release percentiles.
Release-candidate publication grants no Fawn product claim until eligible K0 shared tasks and the local-persistent suite complete under the separate comparison law.
blockers: The historical compact diagnostic archive manifest is not retained in the repository and cannot be used as evidence.
The retained Linux archive is a compact diagnostic archive and omits required Chromium runtime support files.
The original Chromium checkout and complete build output are not present on this machine.
No unchanged exact-oracle application is yet bound to a clean-install release candidate.
No customer-authorized Cloudflare K0 execution receipt exists for the unchanged shared-task application.
No public archive, repeated lifecycle receipt, concurrency receipt, or memory-growth receipt is claimable.
nextActions: Restore or rebuild the complete Linux Fawn output with the declared release profile and package every required support member.
Run the extracted archive in forced Dawn and forced Doe modes before WebGPU application qualification.
Promote one unchanged exact-oracle application only after lifecycle, fallback, hardware identity, replay, and percentile gates pass.
Bind the unchanged shared-task application and exact response oracles, then run the implemented K0 connector beside A/B/C/D; retain differentiation rows as ineligible rather than Fawn wins.
